2027-03-03.title: Wednesday of the Third Week of Lent
readings: Observe the statutes diligently: this will show your wisdom to the peoples
I have come not to abolish the law but to fulfil it. Whoever does and teaches the commandments will be called great
2027-03-03.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet. On any weekday of this third week, especially where there are catechumens, the Mass of the Samaritan woman may be used instead: Exodus 17:1–7; Psalm 95; John 4:5–42.
2027-03-03.verse: Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
theo: Moses stands on the edge of the promised land and speaks to a people about to enter it. He does not hand them a burden; he hands them a treasure. “Give heed to the statutes and ordinances that I am teaching you… so that you may live.” The law of God is for life. And it is a sign to the nations: when other peoples see how Israel lives, they will say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and discerning people!” Then Moses names the real wonder: “For what other great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him?” The commandments are not the rules of a distant lord; they are the words of a God who has come near. That is why Moses ends with a warning and a duty: do not forget what your eyes have seen, and “make them known to your children and your children's children.” Faith is handed on in families, by memory and by example. The Psalm sings the same joy: God “declares his word to Jacob… He has not dealt thus with any other nation.”

In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus says something that must have surprised his hearers: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.” Not one letter, “not one stroke of a letter,” will pass away until all is accomplished. Jesus does not throw away the law given through Moses; he brings it to its full meaning, from the outside to the inside, from the act to the heart, and above all he fulfils it in his own person, by his perfect obedience to the Father unto the cross. The Church has always taught that the moral law of the Ten Commandments still binds Christians, now lived in the freedom of the Spirit and the love of Christ. And Jesus adds a word for every parent, catechist and priest: “whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.” Doing comes before teaching. In the middle of Lent this is a good day to ask: do I know God's commandments, do I keep them with love, and am I passing them on to the next generation by my life?
outline: Ask: what is one rule your parents gave you that you now understand was for your good?
The commandments as a treasure, not a burden.
Point 3 · Not to abolish but to fulfil
Jesus brings the law to its heart.
“Whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.”
live: Make them known to your children (Deuteronomy 4:9)
Tonight, teach a child or grandchild one commandment and tell them why it makes life good.
Keep perfectly one small commandment today that you usually take lightly, such as honest speech or Sunday rest.
2027-03-03.prayer: Lord our God, you are near to us whenever we call on you, and you have given us your law as a lamp for our path. Help us to keep your commandments with love, as Jesus fulfilled them, and to hand on the faith to our children by word and by example. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Jesus fulfilled the law by offering himself in perfect obedience to the Father. At every Mass that same obedient love is made present on the altar, and God comes nearer to us than Moses ever dreamed.

quick: Moses taught Israel that God's law is for life, and that no nation has a God so near.
Jesus came not to abolish the law but to fulfil it.
Those who do and teach the commandments will be called great in the kingdom.
2027-03-03.action: Teach one child one commandment today, with a story from your own life.
2027-03-03.question: Do I see God's commandments as a burden, or as the words of a God who is near?

family.explain: Moses told the people: no one has a God as close as ours! He gave us good laws to help us live well. Do not forget what God has done, and tell your children and grandchildren. Jesus came to help us keep God's law with love.
family.intention: We pray for parents, grandparents and catechists who teach the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of the Ten Commandments do we find hardest at home, and how can we help each other keep it?”

illus: In a family in Changanassery the grandmother had a habit: every evening after the rosary she told the children one short story about a commandment. Lying, stealing, honouring parents, keeping Sunday holy. The children laughed at her old-fashioned examples. Twenty years later, a granddaughter working abroad was asked by her manager to sign a false report. She said: I could hear Ammachi's voice telling me the story of the boy and the false weighing scale. She refused, and kept her job anyway.

pm.open: Lord, you are near whenever we call on you. Write your law on our hearts and help us to live it with joy. Amen.
share: For what other great nation has a god so near to it…? (Deuteronomy 4:7). When have I felt God near to me?
Make them known to your children and your children's children (Deuteronomy 4:9). How am I handing on the faith?
I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). Which commandment does Jesus want to bring to its full meaning in me?
interc: For parents and grandparents, that they may hand on the faith by word and example.
For catechists and teachers of religion.
For lawmakers, that the laws of nations may respect the law of God written in human hearts.
For young people who find God's commandments hard to understand.
For our group, that we may do what we teach.
pm.close: Father, your word runs swiftly and your law gives life. Make us doers of your word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Moses says to Israel: give heed to the statutes and ordinances that I am teaching you… so that you may live (Deuteronomy 4:1). God's law is not a cage; it is the way of life.

And Moses names the real wonder: what other great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him? (Deuteronomy 4:7). The commandments are the words of a God who has come close to his people. And he adds: make them known to your children and your children's children.

Jesus says: do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). He does not cancel the commandments. He takes them to the heart, and he fulfils them by his own obedience, all the way to the cross.

Then he says: whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:19). First do, then teach. Parents, grandparents, catechists: our children learn the commandments more from our lives than from our lessons. This Lent, let us keep God's law with love and hand it on with joy. Amen.
kids: Children, God gave us his commandments like a loving father gives rules to keep his children safe and happy. Jesus kept all of God's commandments perfectly because he loved his Father. Let us learn one commandment today and keep it with love!

intro: Theme: “I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.”
The law that gives life, the God who is near, and the Son who fulfils it all.

sub: Wisdom in the sight of the nations.
q: He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and ordinances to Israel. He has not dealt thus with any other nation;
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one commandment that has protected you or your family.

q: For what other great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call to him?
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
points.apply: Read a short passage of Scripture with your family each evening for the rest of Lent.

points.h: Not to abolish but to fulfil
sub: Not one stroke of a letter.
From the act to the heart.
q: No, the word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart for you to observe.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one “least” commandment you neglect and keep it faithfully this week.

concl: God's law is the gift of a God who is near.
Jesus fulfils it, and asks us to do and to teach.
2027-03-03.resolve: Teach one commandment to a child this week, first by keeping it yourself.
